title: Beta Drugs Limited secures COFEPRIS certification for select oncology products, strengthens its position in ..
thbAction: Position THB's pharma CRM and omnichannel HCP engagement workflows to support launch planning, KAM orchestration, and compliant follow-up across India and the Middle East.
contentHtml:
Beta Drugs Limited has announced that it has received its COFEPRIS certification from Mexico’s health regulator — covering 48 oncology formulations across injectables, oral solids, and oral suspensions. It is the latest in a methodical march by the Panchkula-based oncology specialist to transform itself from a domestic manufacturer into a globally credentialed partner of choice for oncology therapeutics.

Just days earlier, on November 19, Beta had announced a joint venture with Algeria’s IMGSA Groupe SPA to establish IMGSA Oncologie SPA — an oncology manufacturing and marketing company in North Africa. Beta will hold 49% equity in the venture, invest USD 3 million over three years. Crucially, despite being the minority equity partner, Beta will exercise operational control. The JV will acquire IMGSA’s existing oncology plant and product registrations.

Advt

The two announcements, within a week of each other, tell the story of a company that has quietly but systematically built the regulatory and operational infrastructure needed to compete on the global oncology stage.

The Certification Trail

The company’s oncology manufacturing facilities now carry approvals from ANVISA (Brazil), INVIMA (Colombia), and COFEPRIS (Mexico) — three of Latin America’s most stringent regulators. It holds PIC/S certification and EAEU approval and has been working toward EU GMP certification to unlock European markets.

“Receiving the COFEPRIS certification is a significant milestone for Beta. It is a testament to our unwavering commitment to global quality standards.” — Rahul Batra, Managing Director

Each certification is not merely a market access ticket — it is a signal to potential partners, contract manufacturing clients, and institutional buyers that Beta’s quality systems can withstand scrutiny from regulators that sit alongside the FDA and EMA in the global hierarchy of health authorities.

The Bigger Picture

Beta Drugs has come a long way from its incorporation in 2005 as a CMO. Today, the company is present in over 46 countries, holds more than 500 oncology product registrations and supplies to 85% of India’s major corporate and government hospitalsRevenue has been scaling — H1 FY27 revenue stood at Rs 263 crores, representing 29% year-on-year growth — with exports contributing a little over 15% of the top line and growing. The company operates across branded formulations, contract manufacturing (CDMO), exports, and oncology APIs, with backward integration into API manufacturing through its subsidiary Adley Lab Limited.

Advt

The strategic direction is clear: build global regulatory credentials, deepen the product portfolio (currently spanning oncology, IVF, and dermatology), and progressively move from pure-play exports to in-market partnerships. The COFEPRIS certification opens Latin America’s second-largest pharmaceutical market — Mexico’s oncology drugs market alone is valued at approximately USD 3.4–3.7 billion and growing at 10–11% annually. The Algeria JV opens a manufacturing foothold in Africa and the MENA region.

Partner of Choice

What ties these moves together is a consistent thesis: Beta is positioning itself not just as a product company, but as a platform partner for oncology — a company that can offer regulatory dossiers, manufacturing know-how, technology transfer, and quality-assured supply to partners across geographies.

Advt

“This milestone is not just about market access — it is about trust.
